newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan says June inflation jump a quirk.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan says June inflation jump a quirk.

text.p: A sharp rise in a key Brazilian inflation index in June was an oddity that will not change forecasts for seven percent inflation this year, Finance Minister Pedro Malan said Tuesday.

"It was perfectly explainable by seasonal factors and reflects changes in public tariffs that occurred that month and they won't be repeated this month," Malan told the Good Morning Brazil television program.
Malan was referring to the Fipe inflation index, which posted 1.42 percent inflation in June, the highest monthly figure in 14 months and up from 0.55 percent in May.
Higher telephone rates and bus fares were largely to blame for the hike, Fipe economists said.
Fipe, which is one of the country's leading inflation indices, measures consumer price activity in the greater Sao Paulo area. Malan said its limited scope was also reason not to be alarmed.
"It is important to note that inflation in one month in one city in Brazil is not such a big thing for the entire country," he said.
The minister said official and private forecasts continue to see seven percent inflation in 1997, down from about 10 percent in 1996 and 22 percent in 1995.
"And it will be even lower in 1998," he said.
Brazil's Real Plan, which completed its third anniversary last week, is credited with taming hyperinflation through high interest rates and a strong currency.
